Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,

  1
 closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 12pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be summarized
by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City Council and will
also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be recorded for
public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers first. After all speakers in the Chambers have spoken,
the Presiding Officer will call upon those participating via zoom or teleconference.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, virtually, email, phone call, mail and any other method which may become
available. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such times when a State of
Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an

  8
 Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

SUBJECT:  ORDINANCE  GRANTING  A  FRANCHISE  AGREEMENT  TO  PACIFIC
PIPELINE  SYSTEM,  LLC.

PURPOSE:  To adopt  an ordinance  granting  a franchise  renewal  to Pacific  Pipeline  System,  LLC.,
("PPS")  for their  existing  oil pipeline  known  as Pipeline  No. 063 ("Pipeline  063"),  for a 10-year  term.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Adopting  Ordinance  No.  2024-03-CC  granting  a ten-year  franchise  from  April  9, 2024,  through
  and including  April  8, 2034, to Pacific  Pipeline  System,  LLC.,  to use, maintain,  repair  and replace
  a single  pipeline  beneath  specified  public  streets,  together  with  related  appurtenances,  for
  transmitting  and distributing  oil and oil products,  within  the City;  and
  b.  Appropriating  the fees estimated  in the amount  of $24,348  to the General  Fund Reserve.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  If the City  Council  adopts the Ordinance  granting  the franchise  agreement,  PPS will
pay the City  a one-time  granting  fee and annual  fees, as summarized  below.

  Annual  Fees  Granting  Fee  Total

  Year  I  $1,100  $12,943  $14,043

  Year  2 to 10  $1,145  *$10,305
  Total  $2,245  $12,943  $24,348
  * Assumes  an annual  CPI ixicrease  of 2%.

There will  be an increase  in revenue.  The annual  amount  received  under the previous  franchise  agreement
was $1,000  average  per year for a grand  total  of $21,717  including  the Granting  Fee. Negotiations  have
increased  that amount  to $1,100  per year plus  an aru'iual  CPI increase  for  a total  estimated  revenue  of
$24,348  inclusive  of a CPI increase  and granting  fee.

The granting  fee is consistent  with  Section  13.10.010  (Rates - General),  of Chapter  13.10 (Compensation),
Division  1(Oil,  Gas, and Water  Pipelines),  of Title  13 (Franchises)  of the South  Gate Municipal  Code.
The annual  rate is set in compliance  with  California  Public  Utilities  Code 6231.5  subsection  (e)(2),  which
applies  to utility  pipelines  that are not publicly  owned.  It authorizes  an aru'iual franchise  fee in an amount
agreed to by the applicant  and the municipality,  or an annual  franchise  fee computed  by multiplying  the

feet of the pipe within the public streets, ways, alleys, or other public places within the municipality.

agreement for the pipeline located on Miller Way, between Garfield Avenue and Vinvale Terminal, which
was granted under Ordinance No. 2321. Before the City can award a franchise, the California Public

The proposed Franchise Agreement is identical to the current Franchise Agreement except for its effective
period, term, and fees. Highlights of the proposed Franchise Agreement include:

  The Pipelines carg gasoline and diesel products, and are the only pipelines owned by PPS within the

 BACKGROUND:  PPS  owns  and  operates  two  existing  pipelines  in the  City  ("Pipelines").  The
Pipelines  carg  gasoline  and diesel  products  and have been in place  since at least 1994.  They  have been

by separate  franchises,  as follows:

  @  Pipeline  No. 063 is covered  under  Ordinance  No. 2321.  This ten-year  ordinance  was adopted  on

  *  Pipeline  No. 2000 is covered  under  Ordinance  No. 2337. The franchise  expires  on September  13,

  all purposes.

  assignment  shall not be unreasonably  withheld;  or

  by  law  shall  purchase  the Franchise  area,  as described  in  Section  1(B)  by  voluntary
  agreement,  or shall  condemn  and take  the Franchise  area under  the power  of eminent
  domain;  or the Franchise  is forfeited  by the Grantee  due to the Grantee's  noncompliance
  with  the terms and conditions  of the Franchise.

  Franchise,  file with  the City  Clerk  a written  acceptance  of the terms and conditions  of this
  Ordinance:  provided,  however,  that  as to franchises  granted  to the  United  States  of
  America,  use will  constitute  acceptance.

SECTION  9:  Permits.  The  Grantee  shall  obtain  an excavation  permit,  and  pay  the
applicable  fee therefore,  prior  to cornmencing  any excavation  in the right-of-way.  The Grantee
may  obtain  an excavation  permit  by  filing  a set of excavation  plans  with  the City  Engineer,
which  plans  shall  be subject  to the City  Engineer's  review  and approval.  The excavation  plans
shall  show the location  of the proposed  excavation,  as well  as the location  of all known  existing
pipes,  sewers,  conduits,  improvements  and  other  facilities  in  or under  any  Street  or public
property  in which  the franchise  property  is located  with  an adequate  description  of the proposed
work,  including  an estimate  of the  duration  of the  interference  with  any  street  traffic.  The
issuance  of  any  excavation  permit  for  the  construction  or installation  of  a pipeline  for  the
transmission  of  flammable  or combustible  liquids,  gases  or hazardous  materials,  shall  be as
prescribed  by the fire  Chief  of the Los  Angeles  County  Fire  Department  in accordance  with
Chapter  13.14,  Division  1, of Title  13 of the South Gate Municipal  Code.
  A)  Where  it is necessary  to lay underground  pipes through,  under  or across any portion  of a
  paved  or macadamized  street,  such work,  where  practicable  and economically  feasible,
  shall  be done by a tunnel  or bore  so as not to disturb  the foundation  of such paved  or
  macadamized  street.  If the same cannot  be done,  or if it is necessary  to cut the street in
  order to access existing  pipes and appurtenances,  such work  shall be done pursuant  to an
  excavation  permit,  as provided  in above  paragraph,  to be issued  by the City  Engineer
  upon application,  therefore.
  B)  All  work  shall  be subject  to inspection  by the City  Engineer.  All  street  coverings  or
  openings,  valves,  vaults  and manholes  shall at all times  be kept flush  with  the surface  of
  the  streets;  provided,  however,  that  vents  for  underground  vaults  and manholes  may,
  subject  to the prior  approval  of the City  Engineer,  extend  above the surface  of the streets
  when  such vents  are located  in parkways,  between  the curb  and the property  line.  The
  Grantee  shall  provide  adequate  traffic  safety  barriers,  signs,  devices  and traffic  safety
  warning  equipment  in accordance  with  City  ordinances,  rules  or regulations,  and shall
  comply  with  such additional  safety measures  as the City  Engineer  may direct.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION  DECLARING  A  CONTINUED  EMERGENCY  AND
AUTHORIZING  REPAIR,  REPLACEMENT  OR  MAINTENANCE  ACTIVITIES  OF
PUBLIC  FACILITIES  RELATED  TO  THE  URBAN  ORCHARD,  CITY  PROJECT  NO.
539-Pa  WITHOUT  PUBLIC  BIDDING,  PURSUANT  TO  THE  EMERGENCY
CONTRACTING  PROCEDURES  OF  THE  SOUTH  GATE  MUNICIPAL  CODE  AND
THE  CALIFORNIA  PUBLIC  CONTRACT  CODE

PURPOSE:  To declare  an emergency  still  exists  and to authorize  the repair,  replacement  or
maintenance  activities  of public  facilities  related  to the Urban  Orchard  Project  without  public
bidding.  The  Los  Angeles  County  Department  of  Public  Health,  Solid  Waste  Division
("County")  issued  a Corrective  Action  Order  requiring  construction  to stop on the project.  The
declaration  of  emergency  is necessary  to  streamline  the  process  to  procure  a replacement
contractor  to provide  maintenance  activities  to preserve  the site in a safe condition  until  the
County  authorizes  construction  work  on the project  to resume.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider  making  a finding  and adopting
a Resolution  declaring  an  emergency  still  exists  and  authorizing  repair,  replacement  or
maintenance  activities  of public  facilities  related  to the Urban  Orchard,  City  Project  No.  539-
PRK,  without  public  bidding,  pursuant  to the emergency  contracting  procedures  of the South
Gate Municipal  Code and the California  Public  Contract  Code.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no  impact  to the  General  Fund.  The  Urban  Orchard  Project
("Project")  has received  a total of $30.5 million  in grant and other funds  for design,  construction,
operations,  and maintenance,  as summarized  below.

ANALYSIS:  The Project  was under  constniction  and approximately  90% of construction  work
has been  completed.  On  December  29,  2022,  the  City  received  a Corrective  Action  Order
("Order")  from  the County.  The Order  required  the City  to stop all constmction  activities  until
such a time as a Post Closure  Land  Use Plan ("PCLUP")  for the Project  site was approved  by the
County,  Given  the PCLUP  approval  process  and  input  received  to date,  it will  take  at least
several months,  possibly  six or more,  to obtain  approval.

To  avoid  the  significant  delay  damages  that  would  be payable  by  the  City  to the  general
contractor  during  a prolonged  suspension  of the project  pending  approval  of the PCLUP,  the City

  1
  42
 Council  terminated  the general  contractor's  agreement  at a Special  City  Council  meeting  on
February  6, 2023.  Such termination  provided  both  immediate  and long-ternn  cost savings  to the
City  but also created  an immediate  need for the City  to retain  an interim  contractor  to perform
certain  ongoing  maintenance  and safety  activities;  a need which  must  be met  sooner  than  the
time necessary  to engage in normal  public  bidding  procedures

The proposed  Resolution  declares  a continued  emergency  exists pursuant  to the authority  granted
by South Gate Municipal Code 83 l.54.470 and California Public Contract Code 8322050. Those
Code  Sections  allow  cities,  by  resolution,  to approve  the City's  entry  into  contracts  without
engaging  in public  bidding  where  certain  emergency  conditions  are found  to have occurred.  Staff
continues  to believe  that the County's  Order  directing  all construction  work  to be ceased on the
Project,  constitutes  such an emergency  due to the public's  safety with  an unfinished  construction
site and the need to respond  accordingly  to additional  directives  given  by the County  related  to
ensuring  public  safety.  Staff  are  recommending  that  the  City  Council  adopt  the  proposed
Resolution  so that the City  can avail  itself  of the accelerated  contracting  procedures  authorized
by  those  Code  Sections.  The  Resolution  (1)  declares  an emergency,  (2)  authorizes  the  City
Manager  to take  such  actions  deemed  necessary  to  cause  the  maintenance  activities  to  be
performed  and to procure  the necessary  equipment,  services,  and supplies  all without  giving
notice  for bids for contracts,  (3) requires  that at each regularly  scheduled  City  Council  Meeting,
the  City  Manager  present  to the  Council  the reasons  justifying  why  the emergency  will  not
permit  a delay resulting  from  a competitive  solicitation  for bids, why  that action  is necessary  to
respond  to the emergency,  and that the City  Council  review  the emergency  action  to determine,
by a four-fifth's  vote,  that there is a need to continue  the emergency  action  until  the emergency
action  is terminated.

The  City  is working  diligently  to secure  the PCLUP  approval.  Since  the original  Resolution
declaring  an emergency  was approved  by the City  Corincil  on February  6, 2023,  the following
contracts,  expenditures,  and milestones  have been undertaken:

  1.  NR Development  Inc., was informed  that Contract  No. 2021-66-CC  was terminated  by
  the City  Council  effective  February  13, 2023,  except  for maintenance  activities.  As of
  February  16, 2023,  NR  Development  Inc.,  is no longer  providing  any project  services
  or  maintenance  activities,  with  the  exception  of  those  required  in  the  settlement
  agreement.

  2.  Approved  a funding  increase  for TPL  in the amount  of $50,000.  On January  24, 2023,
  the City  Council  approved  a $250,000  budget  for Amendment  No.  6 to Contract  No.
  3352 with  TPL;  however,  Amendment  No. 6 had a budget  requirement  of $300,000.  A
  budget  increase  of $50,000  was administratively  approved  to align  the amount  of the
  budget  authority  with  the $300,000  budget  requirement  for Amendment  No.  6, which
  provides  funding  for the technical  services  required  to comply  with  requirements  from
  the LEA.

  3.  The LEA  has approved  the Summary  of Investigations  Report,  Workplan  of Interim
  Control  Measures  ("WICM"),  Supplemental  WICM  and  Phase  II  Workplan.  The
  WICM  safety measures  were completed  May  of 2023.

BACKGROUND:  The Project  is a part of the FY 2023/24  Capital  Improvement  Program.  The
Project  is located  between  the Los Angeles  River,  Firestone  Boulevard,  the Thunderbird  Villa
Mobile  Home  Park, and the I-710  Freeway.  The two primary  purposes  of the Project  are to divert
and treat stornn water  run-off  from  the Los  Angeles  River  and to install  a new park  to provide
riverfront  recreational  opportunities.

The Project  is being  constructed  on a property  that was used as an unpermitted  landfill  until  1949
by an entity  known  as Southeastern  Disposal  and By-Products.  The property  site is identified  in

 BACKGROUND:  On their  East end, Southern  Avemie  and Southern  Place  front  South  Gate Park
and the LADWP  utility  corridor.  These  areas  have  limited  visibility  from  the general  public  as
compared  to streets  in residential  neighborhoods  and  are therefore  used  for  overnight  parking.
Overnight  parking  activity  is a concern.  The Los Angeles  Fire  Department  Station  54 is located  at
the intersection  of Sorithern  Avenue  and Southern  Place.  Fire  Department  personnel  at that station
requested  that the Cityprohibit  street parking  onthe  portion  of Southern  inthe  vicinity  ofthe  station,
citing  concerns  over  vehicle  break-ins.  Also,  the City  is informed  that homes  just  east of the Fire
Station  have  evening  and overnight  issues  with  people  parking  on Southern  Avenue,  south  of their
homes.  A resident  requested  a preferential  parking  district;  however,  that would  not be allowed  by
the municipal  code,  because  it is not in a residential  community.  Finally,  the Parks  and Recreation
Department  also cited  issues  with  overnight  parking  adjacent  to the South  Gate Park  due to related
activities.

Staff  recommends  that overnight  parking  be prohibited  from  11:00  P.M.  to 6:00  A.M.  as means  to
resolve  the issues.  This  solution  balances  the competing  needs  of South  Gate  residents  relative  to

prohibitions  on overnightparking  on certainportions  of SouthernAvenue  and Southern  Place would
suffice  to minimize  the risk  illegal  activity  while  maximizing  vehicle  parking  available  to City  park
users  during  the park's  normal  operating  hours.  The  City  Council  may  implement  this solution  by
adopting  the proposed  Resolution.

General  Fund, forthe  estimated  cost forthe  consolidated  ofthe  Municipal  Election  withthe  County
of Los Angeles  Primary  Election.  The total  cost ranges  from  $230,000  - $270,000.  Not  included
in the budgeted  election  costs are additional  fees in the case of a Special  Runoff  Election.

BACKGROUND:  Senate Bill 415 mandates that all elections for general  law cities  in
California align with the state's election cycle. In the County of Los Angeles there will be a
general election held on November 5, 2024. Pursuant to SB 415, the City of South Gate having
less than 25% of its voter population casting a vote indicates that tlie City is mandated to align its
General Municipal election with the state's election cycle. As a result, the Los Angeles County
Registrar Recorder/Corinty Clerk's Office is tasked with coordinating all election efforts with the
various cities holding regularly scheduled General Municipal Elections on November 5, 2024.

The Notice of Election will be published before July 15, 2024, once in both English and Spanish
in the Los Angeles WAVE Newspaper and La Opinion to comply with requirements from the
Department of Justice. In addition, copies of said notice shall be posted at Hollydale Library,
Leland R. Weaver Library, and City Hall in both languages, and on the City's website.

The estimated cost to conduct a Special Runoff Election is projected to be higher than that of the
November 5, 2024, General Municipal Election because the City would not be consolidating
election costs with the County of Los Angeles. However, the City Council does have the option
of conducting a Special Runoff Election in-lieu of a coin toss to resolve a tie vote. The chances
of a tie vote are remote; therefore, the need to resolve this occurrence is unlikely.

Section 15651 (a) and (b) of the California Elections Code authorizes the City Corincil,  by a
majority vote, to adopt provisions to require the conduct of a Special Runoff Election to resolve
a Tie vote involving those candidates who receive an equal number of votes and are tied for the
second highest votes for an elective office in the case of the City Corincil. A Special Runoff
Election shall be held only if the City Council adopts a Resolution prior to November  5, 2024;
however, the City Clerk and Election Staff are recommending that a tie vote be resolved using
the Coin  Toss Method.

  acceptable  to the City  Attorney.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no fiscal  impact  from  adopting  the Resolution  approving  the
  comprehensive  successor  Agreement  with  Executive  Management  as all  fiscal  impacts  were
  approved  in the Fiscal  Year 2024/2025  Adopted  Budget.

  BACKGROUND:  Historically,  all Executive  Management  employees  have been covered  by a
  singular,  comprehensive  Agreement,  which  outlined  all benefits  and conditions  of employment
  to which  such  employees  were  entitled.  However,  changes  implemented  in  a previous  city
  management  administration  resulted  in  a different  approach  to how  Executive  Management
  entitlements  shall  be  provided  as new  executive  managers  were  compelled  to  enter  into
  individualized  contracts  rather  than be subject  to a singular,  comprehensive  Agreement.

  While,  in theory,  this  approach  attempted  to slowly  reduce  the benefits  to which  an Executive
  Management  employee  would  be entitled,  some consequences  of this approach  were unforeseen
  and caused  administrative  difficulties.  First,  the degradation  of entitlements  resulted  in a loss of

  1

  67
 entitlements  for any individual  promoting  from  within  the organization,  whether  from  the Police
Management  Association  ("PMA")  to  Chief  of  Police,  or  from  the  Division  Management
Association  ("DMA")  to a Director-level  position.  For the Chief  of Police,  this  caused  him  to
relinquish  his ability  to accrue  an unlimited  amount  of Administrative  Leave,  which  he could
have cashed out upon  retirement.  Instead,  he was forced  to cash out his accrued  Administrative
Leave  bank  prior  to his promotion  from  Police  Captain  to Chief  of Police.  Similarly,  for  the
Deputy  Director  of Parks  & Recreation,  it caused  liim  to be in a perpetual  "Interim  Director"
position  so that he did not lose the entitlements  guaranteed  to him under  the DMA  Memorandum
of Understanding.  This  singular,  comprehensive  Agreement  provides  the necessary  adjustments
to ensure  that  no person  promoting  within  the  organization  from  PMA  or DMA  loses  any
benefits  and/or  entitlements  for  accepting  a higher-level  position.  In  fact,  this  singular,
comprehensive  Agreement  provides  "carve  out"  provisions  to preserve  those benefits  for those
currently  provided  to  legacy  Executive  Management  that  are greater  than  that  of  the  new
Executive  Management  employees,  or restores  some of the benefits  lost by the Chief  of Police  as
a result of his promotion.

Second,  this  comprehensive  Agreement  provides  equity  to  all  positions  in  Executive
Management  to guarantee  consistency  in the benefits  and entitlements.  This  ensures  for greater
ease in the administration  of such benefits/entitlements  as well  as fairness  and clarity  to the
employees  as to what  exactly  the benefits  may be to which  he/she is entitled.  For example,  some
employees  were  receiving  120 hours/year  of Administrative  Leave,  while  others  were receiving
60  hours/year  of  Administrative  Leave,  and  another  was  receiving  50  hours/year  of
Administrative  Leave.  When  compared  to the Administrative  Leave  benefit  a DMA  employee  is
receiving  (80  hours/year  of Administrative  Leave),  some  Executive  Management  employees
were  receiving  less than  that  of their  subordinates.  Additionally,  it should  be noted  that  the
industry  standard  for Executive  Management  employees  in other  cities  ranges  from  100 to 120
hours/year.  To correct  this,  all Executive  Management  employees  will  now  earn 100 hours/year
of Administrative  Leave  and, for two  of the legacy  Executive  Management  employees  earning
120 hours/year,  a carve out is inserted  to ensure that he/she continues  to accrue  at this rate.

Third,  this  comprehensive  Agreement  also  provides  a mechanism  for  those  Executive
Management  employees,  who  are  entitled  to  cash  out  a high  amount  of  accrued  sick  or
administrative  leave  at the time  of separation,  the ability  to receive  this  cash out benefit  over  a
three-year  period  preceding  his/her  retirement.  This  provision  is beneficial  to the City  as well
because it reduces  the financial  impact  of this cash out by spreading  it out over three years.

Finally,  this Agreement  provides  for a pay increase  for Executive  Management  employees  of at
least 4.0%  for  the Chief  of Police  and at least  3.0%  for  the non-sworn  members  (Directors)
effective  the first  full  pay period  of July  2025.  This  pay increase  guarantees  that the Executive
Management  positions  will  be increased  at the same rate as the PMA  or DMA  positions  directly
subordinate  to them.  That  is, all  PMA  members  are entitled  to a negotiated  4.0%  base pay
increase  effective  the first  full  pay period  of July  2024,  and all DMA  members  are entitled  to a
negotiated  3.0%  base pay increase  effective  the first  full  pay period  of July  2024.  However,  the
MOUs  for both  PMA  and DMA  require  their members  to contribute  an additional  1.O% towards
the employer  CalPERS  contribution  as a cost sharing  requirement.  This Agreement  provides  that
Executive  Management  employees  will  also  contribute  an additional  1.O%,  which  shall  be

  2

  68
 effective  on January  1, 2025.  Currently,  Executive  Management  employees  are contributing  1%
toward  the employer  CalPERS  contribution  and this will  increase  it to a total of 2%.

In reaching  the terms  and conditions  of this singular,  consolidated  Agreement,  all Directors  and
the Chief  of Police  had an opportunity  to review  the Agreement  and provide  his/her  input.  The
result  of this  collaborative  effort  between  the City  Manager  and the Executive  Management
employees  is the proposed  Agreement.  To  ensure  that  all Executive  Management  employees
agree with  this Agreement,  each one of the impacted  employees  personally  signed  it; however,
since  the  City  Manager  is the representative  authority  for  all unrepresented  employees,  any
future  iteration  of this Agreement  need only  be signed  by the City  Manager  and approved  by the
City  Council  to be effective.

Finally,  the California  Public  Employment  Retirement  System  (CalPERS)  provides  additional
requirements  for  the  transparency  of  governrnent  and  the  approved  classification/pay  plan.
Pursuant to CalPERS' interpretation of the California Code of Regulations Efi570.5 of the Public
Employees'  Retirement  Law  (PERL),  as outlined  in its  January  8, 2020,  Circular  Letter,  it
recommends  that all CalPERS  employers  maintain  their  classification  compensation  levels  in  one

publicly  available  document,  approved  and adopted  by the governing  body,  which  must  meet all
of the following  criteria:

  l)  Hasbeendulyapprovedandadoptedbytheemployer'sgoverningbodyinaccordancewith
  the requirements  of applicable  public  meetings  laws;

On September  23, 2023,  the City  Council  approved  and adopted  a comprehensive  pay schedule
for all full-time,  part-time,  and elected officials  within  CalPERS  guidelines.  (ResolutionNo.  2023-
62-CC)  Once all negotiated  pay increases  have gone into  effect,  the most recent  iteration  of the
comprehensive  pay  schedule  will  be brought  before  City  Council  for  approval  pursuant  to the
PERL.

Under  the PERL  and the Public  Employees'  Pension  Reform  Act of 2013 (PEPRA),  compensation
earnable  and pensionable  compensation  are determined  in accordance  with  the amounts  identified
on a publicly  available  pay schedule  as adopted  and approved  by the City  Council.  If an employer
were to fail to meet with  requirements  of Section  570.5 as stated above,  the CalPERS  Board  may
determine  at its sole discretion  an amount  that will  be considered  as a pay rate in determining  what
a retiree's  earnable  income  will  be, which  will  never  be higher  than  the amount  stated  on the
comprehensive  salary  schedule.  As  a result,  publicly  available  pay  schedules  are required  by
CalPERS  and are a critical  component  to verify  all members'  pay rates when calculating  members'
retirement  benefits.  Finally,  maintaining  a compliant  publicly  available  pay schedule  will  support
transparency  and expedite  CalPERS'  review  process.  Failure  to provide  CalPERS  with  a compliant
publicly  available  pay schedule  may result  in a retirement  benefit  being  delayed  and/or  reduced.

ANALYSIS:  Although  Resolution  No.  6454  provides  for  a Pay Plan  outlining  the positions
authorized  for City  employment,  there has been the practice  over the years to bring  every  change
to  a position's  job  classification  specification  before  City  Council  for  approval.  However,
Resolution  No. 6454 does not require  such action.  For example,  the City  was prepared  to initiate
the recruitment  for the position  of Housing  Assistant  in the Community  Development  Department
on April  29, 2024; however,  the job classification  specification  needed to be updated  to ensure that
the minimum  qualifications  were  equal  to or less than  the position  superior  to it. While  the
Department  of Human  Resources  and the impacted  union,  MEA,  were able to agree to the changes
quickly,  due to the procedural  requirements  to have this slight  change  approved  by City  Council
pursuant  to a non-stated  requirement  of Resolution  No. 6454, it was not able to get approved  until
the May  28, 2024,  Regular  City  Council  Meeting.  This  process  effectively  caused  a one-month
delay  in initiating  the recruitment  process  for  a crucial  and needed  position  in the Community
Development  Department.

  PURPOSE:  To approve  Amendment  No.  2 to Contract  3396 with  Mr.  C's  Towing  of South  Gate,
  Inc.,  Towing  and Storage  Services.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council will consider:
  a.  Approving Amendment No. 2 to Contract No. 3396 with Mr. C's Towing  of South Gate,
  Inc., for the adjustments of towing and storage fees; and
  b.  Authorizing  the Mayor  to execute Amendment  No. 2 in a form acceptable to the City
  Attorney.

  FISCAL IMPACT:  There is no Fiscal Impact to the General Fund as the increase in fees are
  paid by the owners of towed and stored vehicles.

  ANALYSIS:  On November 28, 2017, The South Gate City Council approved Contract No. 3396
  with Mr. C's Towing of South Gate, Inc., for towing and storage services effective December 23,
  2017 through and including December 31, 2019. This agreement was modified on August 27,
  2019, which extended the term of the agreement for an additional five years, through and including
  December  31, 2024.

  A provision in Contract No. 3396 (Page 7 of 12) Section 302 Subsection E- Fee Limits and
  Posting "Said rates, fees, and charges, shall apply equally to any additional towing and storage
  Contractors with whom the City enters into a contract with to provide Services in the future.  In
  addition, such rates, fees and charges shall be subject to review and modification on the first day
  of each calendar year by the Chief of Police or his designee.

  Since the Contract was awarded in 2017, the fees have remained rinchanged. At the request of Mr.
  C's Towing, a review of the rates was requested due to the increase in operational costs.

was funded  with  $4,120,318  in various  funding  sources,  as summarized  in Attachment  "F."

 ANALYSIS:  Construction of The Boulevard Project is complete, and staff is preparing  to release
 the final  payment  to Sequel  Contractors,  Inc. Public  Contract  Code  Section  7107 establishes  that the

  1  139
 City must accept the completion  of construction  and issue a public  notice  of such prior  to releasing
the  final  payment  on  construction  projects.  The  Notice  of  Completion  ("NOC")  meets  this
reqriirement.  It provides  written  notice  to concerned  parties that all work  on the project  has been
completed.  The NOC  initiates  the 35-day period  within  wliich  concerned  parties  may exercise their
lien rights for the work they performed  on The Boulevard  Project.  The City may use a part, or all, of
the 5% retention  payment  to settle any liens exercised  against the City.  If no liens or claims  have
been filed within 35 days of the filing  of the NOC,  the City  will  release the retention  and any
remaining amounts due to the Contractor.

Contract  No.  2023-10-CC  required  a 5% retention  be held  from  construction  invoice  payments,
which  totaled $170,973  and released within  60 days of completion  of the work.  Construction  will be
completed  on June 7, 2024; thus, the retention  payment  is due August  7, 2024.  However,  the Public
Works  Department  plans  to authorize  release of 50% of the retention  amorint  after  City  Council
approval  of the NOC,  and then release the balance on August  7, 2024.  This is justified  because SCE
is taking  longer  than expected  to schedule  crews to energize  a service pedestal  that was installed  on
The Boulevard  Project.  SCE plans to energize it in July 2024.  This creates a schedule extension  that
is beyond  the contractor's  control.  Further,  tlie schedule extension  does not impact  the status of work
already completed by the contractor  for which  liens  could  be filed.  Withholding  50% retention
would suffice in meeting contract obligations.

On February  14, 2023, the City Council  approved  Contract  No. 2023-11-CC  with  FCG Consultants,
Inc. in the amount  of $208,043  to provide  the construction  management  and inspection  services  for
the construction  of The Boulevard  Project,  with a completion  schedule  of 180 working  days.  FCG
provided  additional  services beyond  the contracted  amount  due to a construction  schedule  extension
of approximately  two (2) months.  The schedule extension  was approved  by the City to provide  time
to complete  construction  of lighting  improvements,  which  were requested  by the City  through  a
change order.  Amendment  No. 1 provided  funding  to compensate  FCG $29,287  for the additional
construction  management  and inspection  services.  The revised  FCG's  contract  amount  including
Amendment  No. l is $237,330.

BACKGROUND:  The Boulevard  Project  was a multi-year  project  that constructed  congestion
relief, safety and deferred  maintenance  improvements  on  Firestone  Boulevard,  Phase  I  was
completed in 2019 and Phase II is now complete.

Phase  II  made  improvements  on Firestone  Boulevard  between  Alameda  Street  and California
Avenue,  and between  California  Avenue  and Annetta  Avenue.  Improvements  included  five  bus
shelters, two bus pull-outs,  street lighting,  sidewalk,  curb and gutter repairs,  pavement  rehabilitation,
traffic  signal  and  street  light  modifications,  ADA  improvements,  road  widening,  storm  drain
improvements,  safety bollards  at the student pickup/drop-off  near South  Gate Middle  School,  and
removal  of humps to resolve  potential  issues adjacent  to South  Gate High  School  and East Los
Angeles  Community  College's  satellite campus.

On February  14, 2023, the City Council  approved  Contract  No. 2023-10-CC  with Sequel Contractors,
Inc. in the amount  of $3,117,454  for the construction  of The Boulevard  Project.  Construction  began
on July 7, 2023,  and will  be completed  on June 7, 2024. The Contractor  has met all the contract
obligations. Work was performed  in accordance  with  the approved  specifications  with  acceptable
quality and worlananship

  2  140
 Two change orders were administratively  approved to complete construction, as follows:

  *  On November 29, 2023, Change Order No. I was administratively approved in the amount of
  $312,000. Improvements included sidewalk, curb ramps, driveways,  and cross gutter
  improvements.

  *  On May 30, 2024, Change Order No. 2 was administratively approved to reduce the contract
  amount by $202,053 for work that was not needed to complete construction.  This change
  order also reconciles the difference between the contract bid quantities and the actual quantity
  of work constructed in the field. It provides $107,361 to fund construction  quantity increases,
  and a reduction of $309,415 for work that was not needed to complete constniction.  The net
  contract reduction is $202,053.

The revised contract amount, inclusive of changes orders is $3,227,401.

The City Council may now accept the construction of the Project as complete, and the Notice  of
Completion can now be filed with the Los Angeles County Registrar Recorder's Office.

FCG looks forward to serving the City of South Gate to complete The Boulevard Phase n Project (No. 476-TRF).
As previously discussed, the FCG budget for Constniction Management, Inspection, and Labor Compliance
services (Services) for the subject project has been drawn down quicker than anticipated due to the inspection
changes requested by the City of South Gate (City). Prior to FCG being awarded a contract for the Services, the
City requested that FCG budget for a 4-hour inspection day, which FCG complied with. After constniction began,
the City asked FCG to perform full-time inspections at 8 hours per day and any overtime in order to closely monitor
traffic and safety throughout the entire work day, and ensure traffic control and safety devices were adequately  set
up at the end of each work day. FCG complied with this request and has provided full-time inspection throughout
the entire duration of the project. Additionally, the City requested end-of-day safety reports outlining the condition
of the site after all crews had left for the day.

The City has also approved added work which includes the installation of 60 uplights within the parkway and
median along Firestone Boulevard which will require additional Constnuction Management, Inspection, and Labor
Compliance services.

Due to the requested changes noted above, the FCG Services budget has a balance of -$8,080.38 as of January 31,
2024.

The remaining work on the project includes (1) Punch List, (2) Uplighting Installation, and (3), Project Closeout.
In order to manage the existing City budget, the City has asked FCG to only perform inspections for the uplighting
at "Critical Milestones" wmch the City has defined as:

  Inspection of material when it arrives on site and discussions of the work plan with the contractor.
  Inspection of lighting foundations after the foundations have been poured.
  Inspection of uplighting after the lights have been set in the foundations.
  Final inspection after all landscaping has been installed.

In order to accommodate the City's request, FCG has budgeted for a total of 24 inspection hours for the uplighting
work. Note that tis  precludes FCG from inspecting  daily traffic  control, safety, laborer hours, unforeseen field

Typica  Issues

The FCG Team understands construction especially on busy
arterials such as Firestone Blvd as we have previously worked on the
same roads with neighboring cities such as Norwalk, Downey,
Whittier, and Irwindale. Such projects with similar features have
similar challenges, specific and typical. Based on the team's
construction experience, here are some of the typical and general
issues for this project and FCG team's approach are discussed
below:

  *  Maintain Traffic Flow
  The FCG Team understands that staging construction of
  work will require lane closures thatmay cause a lot oftraffic delay. These closures will need many signs in advance ofclosure
  in order for residents pre plan for daily trips to minimize inconvenience and complaints. The FCG Team recommends
  Installation of project information signs two-weeks in advance of work; distribute flyers with potential detour routes to

  *  Storm Water Pollution Prevention Program (SWPPP)

 fund  Sorithern  California  Edison  Service  Request  No.  7590554408  which  is necessary  to secure
 dedicated  service  to the South  Gate Police  Station  required  as a part  of the South  Gate Police
 Department  HVAC  System,  City  Project  No. 667-GEN,  in the amount  of $64,724.

 7590554408  is in the amount  of $64,724  and will  be funded  with  the General  Funds budgeted  in
 Fiscal  Year 2023/24  Capital  Improvement  Program  ("CIP").

 the  police  station's  existing  Heating,  Ventilating  and  Air  Conditioning  (HVAC)  system  is
 proposed  to be replaced  and upsized  to meet the demands  for cooling  during  the summer  season.

 service  and electrical  meter,  and modifications  to their  facilities  such as to transformers.  SCE is

 that they perform  the work,  which  is to be funded  by customers,  in this case, the City.

 BACKGROUND:  The  South  Gate Police  Stations  is equipped  with  an aging  HVAC  System.
 The HVAC  System  is composed  of a central  system,  a separate  HVAC  system  serving  the jail
 area, and other  separate  components  serving  other  areas of the station.  It was installed  over  30
 years  ago and has exceeded  its service  life.  The  HVAC  system  is unreliable  and experiences
 failures.  The  Project  proposes  to  replace  the  HVAC  System's  central  components  The

SUBJECT:  ANNUAL  ST ATEMENT  OF INVESTMENT  POLICY

PURPOSE:  To obtain  approval  by the City  Council  of the City's  Annual  Statement  of Investment
Policy.  California  Government  Code  Section  53646  requires  staff  to  annually  submit  the  City's
Statement  of Investment  Policy  to the City  Council.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City  Council  will  consider  adopting  the City's  Annual  Statement
of Investment  Policy.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  None.

ANALYSIS:  None.

BACKGROUND:  California  Governrnent  Code  Section  53646  reqriires  the City  Council  to annually
adopt an investment  policy.  This policy  was written  and adopted  in December  2004,  and affirmed  each
year thereafter.

The  City's  investment  policy  continues  to be very  conservative,  authorizing  only  those  investments
provided  for in the Government  Code.  The policy  requires  diversification  of the City's  investments,
with  no maturity  exceeding  five years, and all brokers  must be pre-screened  before  investing  any of the
City's  funds.

ATTACHMENT:  A. Statement  of Investment  Policy

  l

  216
   Attachment  A

  STATEMENT  OF INVESTMENT  POLICY

POLICY

It is the policy of the City of South  Gate, referred  to as "City,"  to invest  public funds  in a prudent
manner  which  will  provide,  in the  following  order:  1) the  highest  level  of safety  of funds,  2)
liquidity  of funds  in order  that  daily  cash flow  demands  are met,  and  3) that  the  yield  or
investment  return  be maximized,  all while  conforming  to all laws  of the  State  of California
regarding  the investment  of public  funds.

In accordance  with  Section  53646  of the  Government  Code,  the  Director  of Administrative
Services,  hereafter  referred  to as "Director",  will annually  render  to the City Council  a Statement
of Investment  Policy.  The Director,  City Treasurer,  City Manager  and the City Council  Finance
Committee  shall review  the policy  on an annual  basis for submission  and approval  by the City
Council.

DELEGATION OF AUTHORI1Y

The City Council,  consistent  with  Government  Code Section  53601,  has retained  investment
authority  and  is  ultimately  responsible  for  all  investment  decisions.  The  authority  for
administration  of the City's investment  program  is vested with the Director  as a general  extension
of the powers  and duties  of the Director  pursuant  to Chapter  1.08 of the South Gate Municipal
code, and further,  pursuant  to the City Council  action  of February  25, 1997.  As administrator  of
the City"s financial  program,  the Director  is assigned  full discretionary  management  of the City's
investments  and shall  report  directly  to the City Council.  The appointment  of the  Director  as
administrator  of the City's  investment  program  shall be annually  reviewed  by the City Council
pursuant  to  the  City's  statement  of  investment  policy.  In the  absence  of the  Director  of
Administrative  Services, the City Council  delegates  the City Manager  as administrator.

SCOPE

The Director  is authorized  to invest  the City's funds  in accordance  with  California  Government
Code Sections 16429.1  and 53601  et seq. This investment  policy  applies  to all financial  assets of
the City. These funds  are accounted  for in the Annual  Comprehensive  Financial  Report  (ACFR),
which  includes  the following  fund types:

@  General  Fund

@  Special Revenue

*  Debt Service

@  Capital  Projects

@  Enterprise

*  Internal  Services

*  Trust and Agency

*  Any new fund created  by the legislative  body, unless specificallyexempted.

  I

  217
 All monies  entrusted  to the  Director  will be pooled  in the portfolio  except  for the  employee's
retirement  funds  which  are administered  separately,  and the  proceeds  of certain  debt  issues
which  are managed  and invested  by trustees  appointed  under  indenture  agreements.

PRUDENCE

According  to Section  53600.3  of the California  Government  Code, the governing  body, or persons
authorized  to make investment  decisions  on behalf ofthe  local agency, are trustees  and therefore
fiduciaries  subject  to  the  prudent  investor  standard.  The  actions  of  the  Director  in the

performance  of his/her duties  as manager  of public  funds shall be evaluated  using the following
prudent  person  standard  applied  in the context  of managing  the overall portfolio:

  Investments  shall be made with judgment  and care under circumstances  then  prevailing,
  which  persons  of prudence,  discretion,  and intelligence  exercise  in the management  of
  their  own affairs,  not for speculation  but for investment,  considering  the probable  safety
  of their  capital  as well as the probable  income  to be derived.

  Investment  officers  acting  in accordance  with  written  procedures  and the  investment
  policy exercising  due diligence  shall be relieved  of personal  responsibility  for an individual
  security's  credit  risk or market  price changes,  provided  deviations  from  expectations  are
  reported  in a timely  fashion  and  appropriate  action  is taken  to  control  adverse
  developments.

OBJECTIVES

In accordance  with Section  53600.5  of the Government  Code, the primary  objectives  of the City's
investment  activities  shall be in priorityorder:

A.  Safety

Safety of principal  is the foremost  objective  of the investment  program.  Investments  of the City
shall be undertaken  in a manner  that  seeks to ensure  the preservation  of capital  in the overall
portfolio.  The City shall seek to safeguard  principal  by a careful  examination  of credit  risk and
market  risk ofindividual  investments.

  1.  Credit  Risk - is defined  as the risk of loss due to failure  of an issuer of a security  and
  shall be mitigated  byinvestingin  only very safe institutions  and by diversifying  the fund
  so that the failure  of any one issuer would  not unduly  harm the City's cash flow.

  2. MarketRisk  -isdefinedastheriskofmarketvaluefluctuationsduetooverallchanges
  in the general  level of interest  rates and shall be mitigated  by limiting  the weighted
  average  maturity  of the City fund to less than fiveyears.

  2

  218
 B.  Liquidity

The investment  portfolio  will remain  sufficiently  liquid to enable  the City to meet all operating
expenditure  requirements  which  might  be reasonably  anticipated.  In order  to  maintain
liquidity,  the  City  will  develop  a laddered  investment  portfolio  with  regularly  scheduled
maturities  and invest  primarily  in securities  with active secondary  or resale markets.

C.  Return  on Investment

The City"s investment  portfolio  shall be designed  with the objective  of attaining  a market  rate
of return  throughout  budgetary  and economic  cycles, taking  into account  the investment  risk
constraints  and the cash flow  characteristics  of the portfolio.  Whenever  possible,  consistent
with  risk limitations  and prudentinvestment  principles,  the City shall make an effort  to achieve
returns  at the market-average  rate of returns.  The market-average  rate of return  is defined  as
the average  return  on three-month  u.s. Treasury  Bills or the Local Agency  Investment  Fund
administered  by the California  State Treasurer.  These indices  are considered  benchmarks  for
lower  risk  investment  transactions  and  therefore  comprise  a minimum  standard  for  the
portfolio's  rate of return.  The investment  program  shall seek to augment  returns  above  this
threshold  consistent  with  risk limitations  identified  herein  and prudent  investmentpolicies.

Because  the  City  operates  the  portfolio  passively,  the  Director  applies  a buy  and  hold
philosophy  to the acquisition  and sale ofindividual  investments.

  COLLATERALIZATION

  Pursuant  to State  Code,  Sections  53651-53667,  depositories  have duties  and responsibilities

  toward  public  monies  on deposit  that  may differ  from  their  duties  relative  to nonpublic  funds.

  California  law requires  public  funds  to be collateralized-the  depository  must  secure  its public

  fund  accounts  by maintaining  with  the  agent  of the  depository  securities  having  a market

  value  of at least  one  hundred  ten  percent  (110%)  of the  value  of the  public  funds  accounts

  (see Government  Code  Section  53652).  If a depository  uses mortgage-backed  securities  as

  collateral  for  public  funds,  the  market  value  of the  securities  must  be at least 150%  of the

  value  of the  public  funds.  A waiver  may  be granted  under  certain  circumstances  or to the

  extent  the City funds  are insured  by the  Federal  Deposit  Insurance  Corporation  (FDIC).

  DIVERSI FICATION

  The City will  diversify  its investments  by security  type  and institution.  With  the  exception  of

  u.s. Treasury  securities,  federal  agency  securities,  overnight  sweep  accounts,  and authorized

  pools (LAIFI no more than 20% of the entity's total investment portfolio will be invested in a
  single  security  type  or 10%  in any one corporate  or bank issuer.

Xll.  MAXIMUM  MATURITIES

  To the  extent  possible,  the  City will  attempt  to match  its investments  with  anticipated  cash

  flow  requirements.  Unless  matched  to a specific  cash flow,  the City will  not directly  invest  in

  securities  maturing  more  than  five  (5) years  from  the date  ofpurchase.

Xlll.  POLICY CONSIDERATIONS

  Any  investment  currently  held  that  does  not  meet  the  guidelines  of this  policy  shall  be

  exempted  from  the  requirements  of this  policy.  The  City  Council  will  be advised  of the

  situation  and  intended  course  of action.  At  maturity  or liquidation,  such  monies  shall  be

  reinvested  only  as provided  by this policy.

XIV.  REPORTING

  SUBJECT:  EXCESS  ORKERS'  COMPENSATION  INSURANCE  POLICY  WITH
  SAFETY  NATIONAL  CASUALTY  CORPORATION

  PURPOSE:  To renew  the City's  excess  workers'  compensation  insurance  policy  with  Safety
  National  Casualty  Company  [Safety  National]  through  Alliant  Insurance  Services,  Incorporated
  [Alliant].

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:
  a.  Approve  an  excess  workers'  compensation  insurance  policy  with  Safety  National,
  through  Alliant  for a one-year  ternn of July 1, 2024, through  July 1, 2025,  with  a premium
  in the amount  of $197,408.
  b.  Authorize  payment,  in the amount  of $197,408,  to Alliant  for the policy  issued by Safety
  National.
  c.  Authorize  the Mayor  to execute  the "Request  to Bind  Coverage,"  "Program  Commitment
  Agreement,"  or similar  contract  in a form  acceptable  to the City  Attorney.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  The  insurance  premiums,  in  the  amount  of  $197,408,  are  paid  with
  General  Funds  and included  in the Fiscal  Year 2024/25  Proposed  Budget.

  ANALYSIS:  None.

  BACKGROUND:  Each year, the City's  insurance  broker,  Alliant,  requests  quotes  on our excess
  workers'  compensation  insurance  policy,  reviews  the proposals,  and assists the City  with  finding
  the best  and most  cost-effective  coverage  to meet  our  needs.  For  the past  three  years,  staff
  recommended  that the City  Council  renew  the excess  workers'  compensation  insurance  policy
  with  Safety  National  through  Alliant.

  Only  one provider  submitted  a proposal  this year:  Safety  National  Casualty  Corporation  (Safety
  National).  Safety  National  offered  very  competitive  Self-Insured  Retention  (SIR)  levels.  A Self-
  Insured  Retention  (SIR)  is an agreed-upon  dollar  amount  in our workers'  compensation  insurance
  policy  that  must  be paid  before  the  insurer  is obligated  to pay  for  any  remaining  workers'

  1

  232
 compensation  claims.  The proposed  SIR for this year's proposal  is $1,000,000  per Police  officer
per Occurrence  (incident)  and $750,000  for all other employees  per occurrence  (incident).

The  annual  premium  with  Safety  National  increased  from  the  current  annual  premium  of
$177,064  to $197,408  ($20,344  increase),  almost  a 12%  increase.  The  proposed  premium  is
based on the City's  loss history  and "hard"  market  conditions,  as evidenced  by only  receiving  a
single  proposal  compared  to  last  year,  where  we  received  three.  In  addition,  the proposed
premium  is based on actual  and projected  City  payroll.  The Fiscal  Year  2023/24  actual  payroll
was  $33,700,705.  The  projected  payroll  for  The  Fiscal  Year  2024/25  is $39,279,858.  This
upward  trend in the premium  (12%)  reflects  the upward  trend of the City's  payroll  (1 7%).

Per Alliant,  Safety  National  is an industry  leader  in W/C  insurance.  The  City  has experienced
consistent  services  from  this  provider  for  the  past  four  years.  Last  year's  23/24  premium
($1 77,064)  experienced  a modest  1.27%  increase  firom the 22/23 premium  ($174,850).  However,
the 12% increase  is primarily  due to a substantial  increase  in the City's  payroll.

Staff  is recommending  to renew  with  Safety  National.  Safety  National  considers  this a premium
discount  for staying  with  them as an existing  customer.

Congress created the NFIP in 1968 in response to the rising cost of taxpayer-funded disaster relief for flood victims and the increasing amount of
damage caused by floods. The NFIP makes federally backed flood insurance available in communities that agree to adopt and enforce floodplain
management ordinances to reduce future flood damage. The NFIP is self-supporting for the average historical loss year. This means that unless
there is a widespread disaster, operating expenses and flood insurance claims are financed through premiums  collected.

Commercial  buildings  or  residential dwellings  owned  by commercial  entities  are considered  commercial  property.  All others  are residential  dwellings

SUBJECT:  PRESENT  CITY  COUNCIL  STRATEGIC  GOALS  AND  PRIORITY  PROJECT
LIST

PURPOSE:  This item was continued  from the Regular  City  Council  Meeting  of May  28, 2024. To
present the City Council Strategic Goals created.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  Receive  Council  Strategic  Goal List and review  proposed  priority
project  list designed to support the City Council  Goal list. Approve  Council  Goals and priority
project  list to set 2024 priorities.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  The Council Strategic Goals and associated priority projects  do not require
additional funding beyond that already proposed in the upcoming 2024-25 budget.

ANALYSIS:  The City Council  directed  the City Manager  to organize  a Strategic  Planning
Workshop  to develop  a Strategic  Plan. The purpose  of this effort is to provide  a focus on the most
important goals that the City Council  has for the Community  to guide City Staff in what they
should focus on.

BACKGROUND:  The City Council,  City Manager,  City Attorney,  and Department  Heads met
on March  28'h, 2024, at the Azelea room to hold a Strategic Planning session. This meeting  was
facilitated  by consultant  Jacob Green. Jacob Green conducted  one-on-one  interviews  with City
Council  members  and the City Manager  prior to the workshop  to help shape the agenda of the day.
The workshop  included  a discussion  on the origins  of the City Council  - City Manager  form of
government, best practices  in City governance,  and the importance  of setting priority  goals to focus
organizational effort.

Priority  Goals - By the conclusion  of the workshop  the Council  had developed  a priority  goal list
that contained six core goals, each with several sub points to describe the specifics  of the goal.
This list is attached and contains the following top six goal areas.

  *  Public  Safety
  *  Fiscal Sustainability
  *  Infrastructure
  *  Community  Outreach  and Engagement

  254
   *  Community/Economic  Development  and Horising
  *  Organizational  Excellence

Over the course  of the coming  year the city will  be ensuring  these goals are top of mind  and
prioritized  when  determining  how to allocate  staffing  resources.

Priority  Projects  - The City  Manager  and Department  Heads reviewed  the Council  priority  goal
list and after discussion  created  a priority  project  list that creates specific  projects  with  assigned
staff and milestone  deliverable  dates to focus efforts  and provide  results.  These projects  are
focused  on furthering  the goals set by the City  Council.  With  limited  staffing  resources  the list
provides  a realistic  assignment  of staffing  resources  with  proposed  timelines  for deliverables  that
staff feel are achievable.

The proposed  list is presented  for City  Council  review  and approval.  If approved  staff will  work
on these projects  and provide  updates  as outlined  in the attached  project  list. The City  Manager
will  provide  a regular  update  to the City  Council  on project  progress  and provide  a presentation  on
that progress  at Council  meetings  each quarter.

SUBJECT:  CITY  OF SOUTH  GATE  ADU  PROGRAM

PURPOSE:  The City  of South  Gate ADU  Program  will  help the City  streamline  and facilitate  the
production  of  Accessory  Dwelling  Units  by  providing  residents  with  permit  ready  and  Garage
conversion  plan sets, workshops,  and one on one homeowner  support.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  Following  the conclusion  of the Report,  the City  Council  will
consider:
  a.  To receive  and file.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  This  program  is  funded  by  the  Department  of  Housing  &  Community
Development  Local  Early  Action  Plan (LEAP)  Grant.  There  is no impact  to the General  Fund.

ANALYSIS:  The  City  of  Soutli  Gate  ADU  Program  will  lielp  increase  the  mimber  of  safe,
accessible,  and affordable  new construction  of ADU's  and Garage  Conversions.  The City  selected  the
arcliitecture  and planning  fiitn  Office  of Office  and Restore  Neighborliood  LA  to prepare  tlie ADU
plans and outreach  materials  in Englisli  and Spanish.  This program  will  lielp the City  meet its strategic
plan goals and create easy and accessible  liousing  options  for residents.

The City will  assist property  owners  who are interested  in constructing  an ADU  or converting  a garage
or portion  of a house into an ADU  but are hesitant  due to a general  lack of knowledge  and familiarity
with  the zoning  and building  codes,  and the development  permitting  process.  The City  will  provide,
plan options  for Accessory  Dwelling  Units  (ADU)  to choose  from,  thereby  saving  the property  owner
the cost of plans and a shorter  permitting  process.  The ADU  plans will  include  one Permit  Ready plan
set for brand  new construction  of a 410 sq ft., one-bedroom,  one bath ADU  and three Standard  Plans
for Garage  Conversion  ADUs  ranging  from  400 to 600 sq ft.

The City  will  provide  bilingual  marketing  materials  and an ADU  guide  that can be used in a public
outreach  campaigns  and workshops  to educate  and inform  the public  of the City's  ADU  program.  The
guide will  contain  the architectural  and construction  plans,  a clearly  labeled  permitting  flowchart,  and
a new ADU  Application  Form.  These materials  are intended  to prepare  interested  residents  from  the
plan check process  to permit  issuance.

The City  will  also provide  technical  support  by helping  interested  homeowners  complete  an intake
form  at engagement  events with  their property  information  to receive  a feasibility  assessment  and get

garage into an ADU  will receive one-on one technical  assistance  and suppoit  using  a garage
conversion standard plan to take the project to permitting.

The goals of the ADU  Program:

  Legalize  illegally  converted  structures  to safe habitable  units;
  Educate homeowners  about ADUs;
  Cut or eliminate  design cost for the homeowners;
  Expedite  the permitting  approval  process;
  Increase Section 8 housing  supply;  and
  Increase Section 8 Lease-ups.
